---

## Step 1. Library loading and global settings

Loads all required R packages, sets global namespace preferences to avoid conflicts between `dplyr` and other packages, defines input/output paths, and creates a `pub_theme` object used consistently across all figure panels for publication-style ggplot formatting.

```{r}
library(DESeq2)
source("/projects/rps/cgsb/gresham/Akriti/wildyeast1/common_analysis_for_all/Agrawal_single_cell_eqtl_cell_cycle/shared_code/wilcox_pvalue_fix.R")  # R 4.6.1 returns p = 0 for two-sided Wilcoxon p < 1e-16
library(tidyverse)
library(pheatmap)
library(circlize)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Sc.sgd.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(Rtsne)
library(vegan)
library(cowplot)
library(patchwork)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)

select <- dplyr::select
filter <- dplyr::filter
first  <- dplyr::first

BASE    <- "/projects/rps/cgsb/gresham/Akriti/wildyeast1/common_analysis_for_all"
OUT_DIR <- "../results"
dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
TABLE_DIR <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables")
dir.create(TABLE_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
set.seed(42)

# Shared font settings: used by pub_theme (ggplot) and by the ComplexHeatmap gpar() calls
PUB_FONT  <- "Arial"
PUB_SIZE  <- 16                 # axis titles, axis labels, legend titles, strips
PUB_SMALL <- 15                 # legend entries
PUB_AXIS  <- 18                 # larger, bold axis text + titles for Panel C, volcano and GO plots
PUB_LABEL <- 13 / ggplot2::.pt  # in-plot text (geom_text / ggrepel) in mm, = 13 pt

pub_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = PUB_SIZE, base_family = PUB_FONT) +
  theme(
    text        = element_text(family = PUB_FONT, color = "black"),
    axis.title  = element_text(size = PUB_SIZE, face = "bold", color = "black"),
    axis.text   = element_text(size = PUB_SIZE, color = "black"),
    axis.line   = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, color = "black"),
    axis.ticks  = element_line(linewidth = 0.35, color = "black"),
    plot.title  = element_text(size = PUB_SIZE, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    legend.title = element_text(size = PUB_SIZE, face = "bold"),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = PUB_SMALL),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    strip.text       = element_text(size = PUB_SIZE, face = "bold", color = "black"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = NA),
    panel.grid       = element_blank(),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin      = margin(10, 12, 8, 10)
  )

# Add to pub_theme for categorical x-axes with long labels (e.g. clade names)
pub_rotate_x <- theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = PUB_SIZE, color = "black",
                                                 angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
```

---

## Step 2. Input preparation: pseudobulk counts, gene ID harmonization, and metadata

Loads the YPD.1 pseudobulk count matrix and converts row names from common gene names to systematic ORF IDs using a custom annotation table, dropping any genes that cannot be mapped. Filters to nuclear standard chromosomes only (removes mitochondrial and Marker features), then rounds counts to integers for DESeq2 compatibility. Builds an ORF-to-common-name lookup table using the custom annotation with SGD as a fallback. Loads strain-to-clade metadata, checks for strains missing clade annotations, enforces that column order in the count matrix matches row order in the metadata (required by DESeq2), and defines a consistent clade color palette used across all panels.

```{r}
raw_counts <- read.table(
  file.path(BASE, "YPD.1/fastlmm/data/pheno_data/pseudobulk_reliable_transcripts_YPD.txt"),
  header = TRUE, sep = "\t", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE, quote = ""
)
cat("Loaded:", nrow(raw_counts), "genes x", ncol(raw_counts), "strains\n")

all_custom_gene_annotations <- read.csv(
  "/scratch/aa9679/SingleCell_cerevisiae/Gene_exp_analysis/yeast_custom_annotations.csv"
)

common_to_orf <- all_custom_gene_annotations %>%
  filter(!is.na(gene_name), !is.na(gene_id)) %>%
  distinct(gene_name, gene_id) %>%
  deframe()

expr_gene_ids <- rownames(raw_counts)
is_orf <- grepl("^Y[A-Z]{2}\\d{3}[WC](-[A-Z])?$", expr_gene_ids)
expr_orf_ids <- ifelse(
  is_orf, expr_gene_ids,
  ifelse(expr_gene_ids %in% names(common_to_orf), common_to_orf[expr_gene_ids], expr_gene_ids)
)
not_converted <- expr_gene_ids[!is_orf & !expr_gene_ids %in% names(common_to_orf)]
rownames(raw_counts) <- expr_orf_ids
raw_counts <- raw_counts[!rownames(raw_counts) %in% not_converted, ]

gene_location <- all_custom_gene_annotations %>%
  filter(type == "CDS", !is.na(gene_id)) %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  summarise(gene_name = first(gene_name), chr = first(seqnames), .groups = "drop")

standard_orfs <- gene_location %>% filter(!chr %in% c("Mito", "Marker")) %>% pull(gene_id)
raw_counts    <- raw_counts[rownames(raw_counts) %in% standard_orfs, ]
raw_counts_mat <- round(as.matrix(raw_counts))
cat("After ORF conversion + chromosome filter:", nrow(raw_counts_mat), "genes\n")

orf_to_name_custom <- all_custom_gene_annotations %>%
  filter(!is.na(gene_id), !is.na(gene_name)) %>%
  distinct(gene_id, gene_name) %>%
  deframe()

orfs_missing_name <- rownames(raw_counts_mat)[!rownames(raw_counts_mat) %in% names(orf_to_name_custom)]
sgd_lookup <- tryCatch(
  AnnotationDbi::select(org.Sc.sgd.db, keys = orfs_missing_name,
                        columns = "GENENAME", keytype = "ORF"),
  error = function(e) data.frame(ORF = character(), GENENAME = character())
)
orf_to_name_sgd <- sgd_lookup %>% filter(!is.na(GENENAME)) %>% distinct(ORF, GENENAME) %>% deframe()
orf_to_name <- c(orf_to_name_custom,
                 orf_to_name_sgd[!names(orf_to_name_sgd) %in% names(orf_to_name_custom)])

strains_sc <- read.csv(file.path(BASE, "StrainsforSC-RNAseq.csv"), header = TRUE)

sample_meta <- strains_sc %>%
  select(strain = Standardized.name, clade = Clades) %>%
  mutate(clade = str_trim(clade)) %>%
  filter(strain %in% colnames(raw_counts_mat)) %>%
  distinct(strain, clade) %>%
  arrange(match(strain, colnames(raw_counts_mat))) %>%
  column_to_rownames("strain")

mat_strains  <- colnames(raw_counts_mat)
meta_strains <- rownames(sample_meta)

missing_meta <- setdiff(mat_strains, meta_strains)
na_clade     <- meta_strains[is.na(sample_meta$clade) | sample_meta$clade == ""]
extra_csv    <- setdiff(strains_sc$Standardized.name, mat_strains)

cat("Strains in raw_counts_mat:      ", length(mat_strains), "\n")
cat("Strains with clade annotation:  ", length(meta_strains), "\n")
cat("Missing from strain sheet:      ", length(missing_meta), "\n")
cat("Present but clade is NA/blank:  ", length(na_clade), "\n")
cat("In sheet but not in matrix:     ", length(extra_csv), "\n")
cat("Distinct clades:                ", length(unique(na.omit(sample_meta$clade))), "\n")

if (length(missing_meta) > 0)
  cat("  -> no metadata row:", paste(missing_meta, collapse = ", "), "\n")
if (length(na_clade) > 0)
  cat("  -> clade missing:  ", paste(na_clade, collapse = ", "), "\n")

stopifnot(identical(meta_strains, mat_strains))

all_clade_levels <- unique(sample_meta$clade)
all_clade_levels <- all_clade_levels[!is.na(all_clade_levels)]
# natural order: 1, 1 (subclade), 2, ..., 26, M1, M2, M3 (instead of 1, 10, 12, ...)
clade_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(str_extract(all_clade_levels, "^\\d+")))
all_clade_levels <- all_clade_levels[order(is.na(clade_num), clade_num, all_clade_levels)]

# 28 hand-checked, maximally distinct colors (no two closer than ~23 CIELAB units),
# replacing the interpolated "Paired" ramp, which gave near-identical neighbouring shades
distinct_clade_palette <- c(
  "#E6194B", "#3CB44B", "#FFE119", "#4363D8", "#F58231", "#911EB4", "#42D4F4",
  "#F032E6", "#BFEF45", "#FABED4", "#469990", "#DCBEFF", "#9A6324", "#800000",
  "#AAFFC3", "#808000", "#FFD8B1", "#000075", "#A9A9A9", "#000000", "#783E6C",
  "#004614", "#9DC3E6", "#8E7CC3", "#19719F", "#C9666A", "#B8860B", "#585246"
)
stopifnot(length(all_clade_levels) <= length(distinct_clade_palette))
clade_colors <- setNames(distinct_clade_palette[seq_along(all_clade_levels)], all_clade_levels)
```

---

## Step 3. Variance-stabilizing transformation (VST)

Applies DESeq2's variance-stabilizing transform to the full count matrix for use in visualization. An intercept-only design (`~ 1`) is used — no model is fit here, this is purely a normalization step. `blind = TRUE` ensures dispersions are estimated without reference to clade labels, keeping the transform independent of the grouping structure being evaluated downstream. The resulting `vst_mat` is the input for Panels A, B, and C. The VST matrix and strain metadata are written to file as source data tables.

```{r}
dds_full <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = raw_counts_mat, colData = sample_meta, design = ~ 1)
vst_mat  <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(DESeq2::vst(dds_full, blind = TRUE))
cat("VST matrix:", nrow(vst_mat), "genes x", ncol(vst_mat), "strains\n")

write.table(sample_meta %>% rownames_to_column("strain"),
            file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2_strain_clade_metadata_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(data.frame(gene = rownames(vst_mat),
                       gene_name = ifelse(rownames(vst_mat) %in% names(orf_to_name),
                                          orf_to_name[rownames(vst_mat)], rownames(vst_mat)),
                       vst_mat, check.names = FALSE),
            file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2_VST_expression_matrix_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
```

---

## Step 4. Per-clade differential gene expression (DGE)

Runs DESeq2 for each clade with at least 2 strains, treating that clade as "focal" and all others as "rest" (one-vs-all design). Clades with only 1 strain are skipped and reported. Significant DEGs are called at padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 0.3. Results are combined across all clades, DEG counts per clade are summarized, and all outputs are written to file. The union of significant DEGs across all clades (`degs_in_matrix`) is used for Panels A and B.

```{r}
run_clade_dge <- function(clade_of_interest, counts_mat, meta,
                          padj_thresh = 0.05, lfc_thresh = 0.3) {
  n_focal <- sum(meta$clade == clade_of_interest, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_focal < 2) return(NULL)

  meta_de <- meta %>%
    mutate(group = factor(ifelse(clade == clade_of_interest, "focal", "rest"),
                          levels = c("rest", "focal")))
  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts_mat, colData = meta_de, design = ~ group)
  dds <- DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
  res <- results(dds, contrast = c("group", "focal", "rest"), alpha = padj_thresh)

  as.data.frame(res) %>%
    rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
    filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
    mutate(
      gene_name = ifelse(gene %in% names(orf_to_name), orf_to_name[gene], gene),
      direction = case_when(
        padj < padj_thresh & log2FoldChange >  lfc_thresh ~ "Upregulated",
        padj < padj_thresh & log2FoldChange < -lfc_thresh ~ "Downregulated",
        TRUE ~ "NS"),
      clade = clade_of_interest, n_focal = n_focal)
}

all_clades <- sort(unique(sample_meta$clade)); all_clades <- all_clades[!is.na(all_clades)]

clade_sizes <- sample_meta %>%
  rownames_to_column("strain") %>%
  filter(!is.na(clade)) %>%
  dplyr::count(clade, name = "n_strains")

singleton_clades <- clade_sizes %>% filter(n_strains < 2)
testable_clades  <- clade_sizes %>% filter(n_strains >= 2)
n_na_clade       <- sum(is.na(sample_meta$clade))

cat("Clades with clade annotation:   ", nrow(clade_sizes), "\n")
cat("  testable (>= 2 strains):      ", nrow(testable_clades), "\n")
cat("  skipped (only 1 strain):      ", nrow(singleton_clades),
    "  covering", sum(singleton_clades$n_strains), "strains\n")
cat("Strains with NA clade:          ", n_na_clade, "\n")

if (nrow(singleton_clades) > 0) {
  cat("\nSingleton clades not tested:\n")
  print(as_tibble(singleton_clades), n = Inf)
}

dge_results <- lapply(all_clades, run_clade_dge, counts_mat = raw_counts_mat, meta = sample_meta)
names(dge_results) <- all_clades
dge_results <- Filter(Negate(is.null), dge_results)
dge_combined <- bind_rows(dge_results)

sig_degs <- dge_combined %>% filter(direction != "NS") %>% pull(gene) %>% unique()
degs_in_matrix <- intersect(sig_degs, rownames(vst_mat))

cat("\nClades tested:", length(dge_results),
    "| unique DEGs across clades:", length(degs_in_matrix), "\n")

deg_counts_per_clade <- dge_combined %>%
  filter(direction != "NS") %>%
  dplyr::count(clade, n_focal, direction) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(Upregulated + Downregulated))
print(deg_counts_per_clade, n = Inf)

sign_deg <- dge_combined %>% filter(direction != "NS")

write.table(dge_combined, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2_clade_DESeq2_all_genes_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(sign_deg, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2_clade_DESeq2_significant_DEGs_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(deg_counts_per_clade, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2_DEG_counts_per_clade_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(clade_sizes %>% mutate(tested = n_strains >= 2),
            file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2_clade_sizes_tested_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
```

---

## Step 5. Panel A — strain-level DEG heatmap (ComplexHeatmap)

Takes the union DEG set, z-scores expression across strains (capped at ±3), and then plots six versions: (1) all strains, (2) clades with only 1 strain removed, (3) the same as (2) with the number of cells per strain (demuxlet singlets) added to each strain label, (4) clades with 2 or fewer strains removed, (5) clades with 3 or fewer strains removed, (6) strains with fewer than 30 cells removed, then clades left with only 1 strain removed (strain labels include the number of cells). Each is a clustered heatmap (Ward.D2 linkage for both rows and columns) with a clade color annotation bar on top; the clade legend lists clades in the order they first appear along the heatmap. Each heatmap is saved as a 600 dpi TIFF, and its clustered row/column order is written to file as source data.

```{r}
vst_degs_strain <- vst_mat[degs_in_matrix, , drop = FALSE]
scaled_A <- t(scale(t(vst_degs_strain)))
scaled_A[scaled_A >  3] <-  3
scaled_A[scaled_A < -3] <- -3

# Clade sizes among strains present in the expression matrix
clade_n <- table(sample_meta[colnames(scaled_A), "clade"])

# extra space between the heatmap titles and the strain names / dendrogram, so the
# "Demuxlet identified strains" title does not overlap the longest (bold) strain names
ht_opt$TITLE_PADDING <- unit(c(6, 2), "mm")

col_fun_A <- colorRamp2(
  c(-3, -1.5, 0, 1.5, 3),
  c("#2166AC", "#92C5DE", "white", "#F4A582", "#B2182B")
)

# Cells per strain = demuxlet singlet droplets (same QC as the pseudobulk step in Fig. 3)
demux_YPD1 <- read.delim(file.path(BASE, "YPD.1/demuxlet/merged_demuxlet_output_YPD.tsv"))
cells_per_strain <- demux_YPD1 %>%
  filter(DROPLET.TYPE == "SNG") %>%
  dplyr::count(SNG.BEST.GUESS) %>%
  deframe()
stopifnot(all(colnames(scaled_A) %in% names(cells_per_strain)))

# Builds the Panel A heatmap for strains whose clade has >= min_strains strains.
# Columns are clustered up front (Ward.D2) so the clade legend can be listed in the
# same left-to-right order in which the clades first appear along the heatmap.
# show_cells = TRUE labels each strain as "STRAIN (n cells)".
# min_cells drops strains with fewer cells first; clade sizes are then counted on the
# remaining strains, so min_strains applies after the cell filter.
make_fig2A <- function(min_strains, show_cells = FALSE, min_cells = 0) {
  pass_cells <- colnames(scaled_A)[cells_per_strain[colnames(scaled_A)] >= min_cells]
  clade_n_kept <- table(sample_meta[pass_cells, "clade"])
  keep_clades <- names(clade_n_kept)[clade_n_kept >= min_strains]
  strains <- pass_cells[sample_meta[pass_cells, "clade"] %in% keep_clades]
  mat <- scaled_A[, strains, drop = FALSE]

  col_hc <- hclust(dist(t(mat)), method = "ward.D2")
  clade_vec <- sample_meta[colnames(mat), "clade"]
  legend_clades <- unique(clade_vec[col_hc$order])
  col_labels <- if (show_cells) {
    paste0(colnames(mat), " (", cells_per_strain[colnames(mat)], ")")
  } else colnames(mat)

  cat("min_cells =", min_cells, "| min_strains =", min_strains, ":", length(keep_clades), "clades,",
      ncol(mat), "strains x", nrow(mat), "genes\n")

  col_ann <- HeatmapAnnotation(
    clade = clade_vec,
    col = list(clade = clade_colors[legend_clades]),
    show_annotation_name = FALSE,
    annotation_legend_param = list(
      clade = list(
        title = "Clade",
        at     = legend_clades,   # legend order = order along the heatmap
        labels = legend_clades,
        title_gp  = gpar(fontsize = PUB_SIZE, fontface = "bold", fontfamily = PUB_FONT),
        labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = PUB_SMALL, fontfamily = PUB_FONT),
        grid_height = unit(5, "mm"), grid_width = unit(5, "mm"),
        ncol = 1   # all clades in one vertical column
      )
    ),
    which = "column"
  )

  ht <- Heatmap(
    mat,
    col  = col_fun_A,
    name = "z-score",
    cluster_rows    = TRUE,
    cluster_columns = col_hc,
    clustering_method_rows = "ward.D2",
    top_annotation    = col_ann,
    show_row_names    = FALSE,
    show_column_names = TRUE,
    column_labels     = col_labels,
    # axis titles: strains along x (below the strain names), DEGs along y
    column_title      = if (show_cells) "Demuxlet identified strains (number of cells)"
                        else "Demuxlet identified strains",
    column_title_side = "bottom",
    column_title_gp   = gpar(fontsize = PUB_SIZE, fontface = "bold", fontfamily = PUB_FONT),
    row_title         = "Differentially expressed genes",
    row_title_gp      = gpar(fontsize = PUB_SIZE, fontface = "bold", fontfamily = PUB_FONT),
    column_names_rot  = 90,
    column_names_gp   = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold", fontfamily = PUB_FONT),  # strain names; ~75 strains, so 12 pt is about the max that fits
    heatmap_legend_param = list(
      title      = "DEG expression",
      title_gp   = gpar(fontsize = PUB_SIZE, fontface = "bold", fontfamily = PUB_FONT),
      labels_gp  = gpar(fontsize = PUB_SMALL, fontfamily = PUB_FONT),
      at         = c(-3, -1.5, 0, 1.5, 3),
      labels     = c("-3 (low)", "-1.5", "0 (mean)", "1.5", "+3 (high)"),
      legend_height = unit(5, "cm")
    ),
    border = FALSE
  )
  list(ht = ht, mat = mat)
}

# Versions of Panel A:
#   all_clades           every strain with a clade annotation
#   min2_strains         clades with only 1 strain removed (the clades tested in DGE)
#   min2_strains_ncells  as min2_strains, strain labels include the number of cells
#   min3_strains         clades with 2 or fewer strains removed
#   min4_strains         clades with 3 or fewer strains removed
#   min30cells_min2_strains  strains with < 30 cells removed, then clades left with
#                            only 1 strain removed; labels include the number of cells
fig2A_versions <- list(
  all_clades          = list(min_strains = 1),
  min2_strains        = list(min_strains = 2),
  min2_strains_ncells = list(min_strains = 2, show_cells = TRUE),
  min3_strains        = list(min_strains = 3),
  min4_strains        = list(min_strains = 4),
  min30cells_min2_strains = list(min_strains = 2, show_cells = TRUE, min_cells = 30)
)

for (v in names(fig2A_versions)) {
  res <- do.call(make_fig2A, fig2A_versions[[v]])

  ht_drawn <- draw(res$ht,
                   heatmap_legend_side    = "right",
                   annotation_legend_side = "right",
                   merge_legend           = TRUE)

  hm_rows <- rownames(res$mat)[row_order(ht_drawn)]
  hm_cols <- colnames(res$mat)[column_order(ht_drawn)]

  write.table(data.frame(gene = hm_rows,
                         gene_name = ifelse(hm_rows %in% names(orf_to_name), orf_to_name[hm_rows], hm_rows),
                         res$mat[hm_rows, hm_cols, drop = FALSE], check.names = FALSE),
              file.path(TABLE_DIR, paste0("Fig2A_heatmap_DEG_zscore_matrix_", v, "_YPD1.txt")),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
  write.table(data.frame(column_order = seq_along(hm_cols), strain = hm_cols,
                         clade = sample_meta[hm_cols, "clade"],
                         n_cells = cells_per_strain[hm_cols]),
              file.path(TABLE_DIR, paste0("Fig2A_heatmap_strain_order_", v, "_YPD1.txt")),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

  tiff(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("Fig2A_strain_DEG_heatmap_", v, ".tiff")),
       width = 16, height = 9, units = "in", res = 600, compression = "lzw")
  draw(res$ht,
       heatmap_legend_side    = "right",
       annotation_legend_side = "right",
       merge_legend           = TRUE)
  dev.off()
}
```


---

## Step 8. GO over-representation analysis (ORA) per clade

Runs GO biological process ORA (clusterProfiler, BH-corrected) separately on the upregulated and downregulated DEG sets for each testable clade, using the full set of tested genes as the background universe. Results are combined across clades and written to file. The ORA output is used in Step 9 to identify which gene regulons (GAL, NCR) show enrichment and therefore which genes to feature in Panel C.

```{r}
run_ora <- function(genes, universe, keytype = "ORF") {
  if (length(genes) < 5) return(NULL)
  enrichGO(gene = genes, universe = universe, OrgDb = org.Sc.sgd.db,
           keyType = keytype, ont = "BP", pAdjustMethod = "BH",
           pvalueCutoff = 0.05, qvalueCutoff = 0.2, readable = FALSE)
}

universe_genes <- unique(dge_combined$gene)
ora_results <- lapply(names(dge_results), function(cl) {
  list(up   = run_ora(dge_results[[cl]]$gene[dge_results[[cl]]$direction == "Upregulated"],   universe_genes),
       down = run_ora(dge_results[[cl]]$gene[dge_results[[cl]]$direction == "Downregulated"], universe_genes))
})
names(ora_results) <- names(dge_results)

ora_combined <- lapply(names(ora_results), function(cl) {
  bind_rows(
    if (!is.null(ora_results[[cl]]$up))   as.data.frame(ora_results[[cl]]$up)   %>% mutate(direction = "Upregulated",   clade = cl),
    if (!is.null(ora_results[[cl]]$down)) as.data.frame(ora_results[[cl]]$down) %>% mutate(direction = "Downregulated", clade = cl)
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()

write_csv(ora_combined, file.path(OUT_DIR, "Fig2_clade_GO_ORA_all.csv"))
```

---

## Step 9. Panel C gene selection — GAL and NCR regulon members

Searches the ORA results for GO terms matching galactose metabolism (GAL regulon) and nitrogen catabolite repression (NCR regulon) by keyword. Genes driving those enriched terms are extracted from the `geneID` field. A canonical gene list for each regulon serves as a fallback if ORA finds no enriched terms. The final focus gene sets are the union of ORA-derived and canonical genes, restricted to genes detected in the count matrix. A source data table recording each gene's origin (ORA hit and/or canonical list) is written to file.

```{r}
gal_hits <- ora_combined %>% filter(str_detect(tolower(Description), "galactose"))
ncr_hits <- ora_combined %>% filter(str_detect(tolower(Description),
                          "nitrogen catabolite|allantoin|urea catabolic|nitrogen compound catabolic"))

cat("GO terms matching GAL regulon:", nrow(gal_hits), "\n")
cat("GO terms matching NCR regulon:", nrow(ncr_hits), "\n")

gal_canonical_names <- c("GAL1","GAL2","GAL3","GAL4","GAL7","GAL10","GAL80")
ncr_canonical_names <- c("MEP1","MEP2","GAP1","DAL5","DUR1,2","DUR3","PUT1","PUT4","GLN1","GLN3","GAT1")

name_to_orf <- setNames(names(orf_to_name), orf_to_name)

resolve_focus_genes <- function(go_hits, canonical_names) {
  from_go <- if (nrow(go_hits) > 0) unique(unlist(str_split(go_hits$geneID, "/"))) else character(0)
  from_canonical <- intersect(name_to_orf[canonical_names], rownames(vst_mat))
  union(intersect(from_go, rownames(vst_mat)), from_canonical)
}

gal_focus_genes <- resolve_focus_genes(gal_hits, gal_canonical_names)
ncr_focus_genes <- resolve_focus_genes(ncr_hits, ncr_canonical_names)
cat("GAL focus genes resolved:", length(gal_focus_genes), "\n")
cat("NCR focus genes resolved:", length(ncr_focus_genes), "\n")

go_genes_of <- function(go_hits) if (nrow(go_hits) > 0) unique(unlist(str_split(go_hits$geneID, "/"))) else character(0)
focus_gene_table <- bind_rows(
  tibble(regulon = "GAL", gene = gal_focus_genes,
         from_GO_ORA    = gal_focus_genes %in% go_genes_of(gal_hits),
         from_canonical = gal_focus_genes %in% name_to_orf[gal_canonical_names]),
  tibble(regulon = "NCR", gene = ncr_focus_genes,
         from_GO_ORA    = ncr_focus_genes %in% go_genes_of(ncr_hits),
         from_canonical = ncr_focus_genes %in% name_to_orf[ncr_canonical_names])
) %>%
  mutate(gene_name = ifelse(gene %in% names(orf_to_name), orf_to_name[gene], gene), .after = gene)

write.table(focus_gene_table, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2C_GAL_NCR_focus_genes_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(bind_rows(gal_hits %>% mutate(regulon = "GAL"), ncr_hits %>% mutate(regulon = "NCR")),
            file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2C_GAL_NCR_matching_GO_terms_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Step 10. Panel B — t-SNE on union DEG set

Runs t-SNE (perplexity = min(15, floor((n-1)/3)), 1000 iterations, seed 42) on the VST expression matrix restricted to the union DEG set. Strains are colored by clade; clade centroids (mean t-SNE coordinates, clades with ≥ 2 strains) are labeled with ggrepel. The plot is saved as a 600 dpi TIFF and t-SNE coordinates per strain are written as source data.

```{r fig.width = 14, fig.height = 7.5}
tsne_input <- t(vst_mat[degs_in_matrix, , drop = FALSE])
set.seed(42)
tsne_res <- Rtsne(tsne_input, dims = 2,
                  perplexity = min(15, floor((nrow(tsne_input) - 1) / 3)),
                  max_iter = 1000, check_duplicates = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)

tsne_df <- data.frame(tSNE1 = tsne_res$Y[, 1], tSNE2 = tsne_res$Y[, 2],
                      strain = rownames(tsne_input)) %>%
  left_join(sample_meta %>% rownames_to_column("strain"), by = "strain")

centroids_B <- tsne_df %>% filter(!is.na(clade)) %>%
  group_by(clade) %>% summarise(tSNE1 = mean(tSNE1), tSNE2 = mean(tSNE2), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 2)

fig2B <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = filter(tsne_df, is.na(clade)), aes(tSNE1, tSNE2),
             shape = 1, size = 2, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(data = filter(tsne_df, !is.na(clade)), aes(tSNE1, tSNE2, color = clade),
             size = 2.3, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = centroids_B, aes(tSNE1, tSNE2, label = clade),
                           size = PUB_LABEL, fontface = "bold", color = "black", family = PUB_FONT,
                           max.overlaps = 20, segment.size = 0.3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = clade_colors, na.value = "grey50", name = "Clade",
                     breaks = names(clade_colors)) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4, alpha = 1), ncol = 2)) +
  labs(x = "t-SNE 1", y = "t-SNE 2") +
  pub_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

print(fig2B)

write.table(tsne_df, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2B_tSNE_coordinates_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "Fig2B_tsne_clade.tiff"), fig2B, width = 14, height = 7.5,
       units = "in", dpi = 600, device = "tiff", compression = "lzw")
```

## Step 11. Panel C — GAL and NCR regulon expression boxplots

For each regulon (GAL: GAL1, GAL2, GAL4, PGM1; NCR: ORA + canonical genes), plots per-strain VST expression as boxplots faceted by gene, with clades on the x-axis colored by the shared clade palette. Each regulon is saved as a separate TIFF sized to accommodate the number of genes (3 per row). Panel C source data (per-strain expression for all plotted genes) is written to file.

```{r fig.width = 16, fig.height = 12}
plot_focus_regulon <- function(genes, title = NULL) {
  if (length(genes) == 0) return(NULL)

  df <- as.data.frame(t(vst_mat[genes, , drop = FALSE])) %>%
    rownames_to_column("strain") %>%
    pivot_longer(-strain, names_to = "gene", values_to = "expr") %>%
    mutate(gene_name = ifelse(gene %in% names(orf_to_name), orf_to_name[gene], gene),
           gene_name = factor(gene_name, levels = unique(ifelse(genes %in% names(orf_to_name),
                                                                orf_to_name[genes], genes)))) %>%
    left_join(sample_meta %>% rownames_to_column("strain"), by = "strain") %>%
    filter(!is.na(clade))

  ggplot(df, aes(x = clade, y = expr, fill = clade)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, linewidth = 0.3) +
    facet_wrap(~ gene_name, ncol = 2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = clade_colors, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = "VST expression") +
    pub_theme +
    pub_rotate_x +
    # bigger axis text than pub_theme (PUB_AXIS, same as the volcano and GO plots)
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = PUB_AXIS, face = "bold", color = "black",
                                     angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = PUB_AXIS, face = "bold", color = "black"),
          axis.title  = element_text(size = PUB_AXIS, face = "bold", color = "black"),
          strip.text  = element_text(size = PUB_SIZE, face = "bold.italic"))
}

gal_panel_names <- c("GAL1", "GAL2", "GAL4", "PGM1")
gal_plot_genes  <- unname(name_to_orf[gal_panel_names])
gal_plot_genes  <- gal_plot_genes[!is.na(gal_plot_genes) & gal_plot_genes %in% rownames(vst_mat)]
cat("GAL panel genes plotted:", paste(orf_to_name[gal_plot_genes], collapse = ", "), "\n")

fig2C_GAL <- plot_focus_regulon(gal_plot_genes)
fig2C_NCR <- plot_focus_regulon(ncr_focus_genes, "NCR regulon (nitrogen catabolite repression) (YPD.1)")

print(fig2C_GAL)
print(fig2C_NCR)

write.table(bind_rows(if (!is.null(fig2C_GAL)) fig2C_GAL$data %>% mutate(regulon = "GAL"),
                      if (!is.null(fig2C_NCR)) fig2C_NCR$data %>% mutate(regulon = "NCR")),
            file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2C_GAL_NCR_expression_per_strain_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

n_row_GAL <- ceiling(length(gal_plot_genes) / 2)
n_row_NCR <- ceiling(length(ncr_focus_genes) / 2)

ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "Fig2C1_GAL_regulon.tiff"), fig2C_GAL,
       width = 16, height = 6 * n_row_GAL,
       units = "in", dpi = 600, device = "tiff", compression = "lzw")
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "Fig2C1_NCR_regulon.tiff"), fig2C_NCR,
       width = 16, height = 6 * n_row_NCR,
       units = "in", dpi = 600, device = "tiff", compression = "lzw")
# vector PDFs for the paper figure
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "Fig2C1_GAL_regulon.pdf"), fig2C_GAL,
       width = 16, height = 6 * n_row_GAL, units = "in", device = cairo_pdf)
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "Fig2C1_NCR_regulon.pdf"), fig2C_NCR,
       width = 16, height = 6 * n_row_NCR, units = "in", device = cairo_pdf)
```

## Step 12. GAL gene normality check

Tests whether VST expression of the four GAL panel genes is normally distributed using the Shapiro-Wilk test, and produces Q-Q plots for a visual check. This informs whether parametric or non-parametric tests are appropriate for inter-clade comparisons of GAL gene expression in subsequent steps.

```{r}
cat("\n=== Shapiro-Wilk normality test (p > 0.05 = normal) ===\n")

shapiro_results <- lapply(gal_plot_genes, function(g) {
  gene_name <- ifelse(g %in% names(orf_to_name), orf_to_name[g], g)
  expr_vals <- as.numeric(vst_mat[g, ])
  test <- shapiro.test(expr_vals)
  tibble(gene = g, gene_name = gene_name, p.value = test$p.value, normal = test$p.value > 0.05)
}) %>% bind_rows()

print(shapiro_results)
cat("Genes that appear normal:", sum(shapiro_results$normal), "/", nrow(shapiro_results), "\n")
write.table(shapiro_results, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2C_GAL_genes_shapiro_normality_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

qq_df <- as.data.frame(t(vst_mat[gal_plot_genes, , drop = FALSE])) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "gene", values_to = "expr") %>%
  mutate(gene_name = factor(orf_to_name[gene], levels = orf_to_name[gal_plot_genes]))

qq_plot <- ggplot(qq_df, aes(sample = expr)) +
  stat_qq(size = 0.8) +
  stat_qq_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ gene_name, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Sample quantiles (VST)") +
  pub_theme

print(qq_plot)
```

## Step 13. GAL1 in-depth: expression by clade and French dairy comparison

Extracts GAL1 (YBR020W) expression per strain, summarizes mean/median/SD by clade, and runs a Wilcoxon rank-sum test comparing the French dairy clade (which visually appears to have high GAL1 expression) against all other clades. Results and test statistics are written to file.

```{r}
gal1_data <- as.data.frame(t(vst_mat["YBR020W", , drop = FALSE])) %>%
  rownames_to_column("strain") %>%
  pivot_longer(-strain, names_to = "gene", values_to = "expr") %>%
  left_join(sample_meta %>% rownames_to_column("strain"), by = "strain") %>%
  filter(!is.na(clade))

cat("\n=== GAL1 expression by clade ===\n")
gal1_summary <- gal1_data %>%
  group_by(clade) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(expr), median = median(expr),
            sd = sd(expr), min = min(expr), max = max(expr), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(mean))
print(gal1_summary)

cat("\n=== French dairy vs Others (Wilcoxon test) ===\n")
gal1_data_grouped <- gal1_data %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(clade == "5. French dairy", "French dairy", "Others"))

french_vs_others <- wilcox.test(expr ~ group, data = gal1_data_grouped)
cat("p-value:", french_vs_others$p.value, "\n")
cat("Mean French dairy:", mean(gal1_data_grouped$expr[gal1_data_grouped$group == "French dairy"]), "\n")
cat("Mean Others:", mean(gal1_data_grouped$expr[gal1_data_grouped$group == "Others"]), "\n")

write.table(gal1_summary, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2C_GAL1_expression_by_clade_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(tibble(gene = "YBR020W", gene_name = "GAL1",
                   comparison = "5. French dairy vs all other clades",
                   test = "Wilcoxon rank-sum",
                   n_french_dairy = sum(gal1_data_grouped$group == "French dairy"),
                   n_others = sum(gal1_data_grouped$group == "Others"),
                   mean_french_dairy = mean(gal1_data_grouped$expr[gal1_data_grouped$group == "French dairy"]),
                   mean_others = mean(gal1_data_grouped$expr[gal1_data_grouped$group == "Others"]),
                   W = unname(french_vs_others$statistic),
                   p_value = french_vs_others$p.value),
            file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Fig2C_GAL1_French_dairy_vs_others_YPD1.txt"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Step 14. Reusable plot functions — volcano and GO dot plot

Defines two publication-ready plotting functions used in Step 15. `plot_volcano()` draws a DESeq2 volcano plot colored by direction (up/down/NS) with ggrepel labels for the top significant genes. `plot_go_dotplot()` draws a faceted dot plot of the top GO BP terms per direction, with strip colors matching the up/down scheme, and returns a gtable (grid grob) with manually recolored facet strips.

```{r}
plot_volcano <- function(res_df, clade_label, padj_thresh = 0.05,
                         lfc_thresh = 0.3, top_n_labels = 15) {
  sig       <- res_df %>% filter(direction != "NS")
  top_genes <- sig %>% arrange(padj) %>% slice_head(n = top_n_labels)
  n_up      <- sum(sig$direction == "Upregulated")
  n_down    <- sum(sig$direction == "Downregulated")

  ggplot(res_df, aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj),
                     color = direction, size = -log10(padj))) +
    geom_point(data = filter(res_df, direction == "NS"),
               alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8, color = "grey80") +
    geom_point(data = filter(res_df, direction != "NS"), alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(padj_thresh),
               linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.35) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-lfc_thresh, lfc_thresh),
               linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.35) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = top_genes, aes(label = gene_name),
                             size = PUB_LABEL, color = "black", fontface = "italic", family = PUB_FONT,
                             max.overlaps = 25, segment.color = "grey60",
                             segment.size = 0.3, box.padding = 0.4,
                             point.padding = 0.3, force = 2) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(Upregulated = "#C0392B", Downregulated = "#2471A3", NS = "grey80"),
      labels = c(Upregulated = paste0("Up (", n_up, ")"),
                 Downregulated = paste0("Down (", n_down, ")"), NS = "NS"),
      breaks = c("Upregulated", "Downregulated", "NS")) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.5, 3.5), guide = "none") +
    # bold() inside expression(): plotmath titles ignore the theme's face = "bold"
    labs(x = expression(bold(log[2]~"fold change (focal vs. rest)")),
         y = expression(bold(-log[10]~"(adjusted"~bolditalic(p)~")")),
         title = clade_label, color = NULL) +
    pub_theme +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4))) +
    # bigger axis text than pub_theme (PUB_AXIS, same as Panel C and the GO dot plots)
    theme(axis.text  = element_text(size = PUB_AXIS, face = "bold", color = "black"),
          axis.title = element_text(size = PUB_AXIS, face = "bold", color = "black"),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.spacing.x = unit(0.3, "cm"))
}

plot_go_dotplot <- function(ora_up, ora_down, clade_label, top_n = 8) {
  df_up   <- if (!is.null(ora_up)   && nrow(as.data.frame(ora_up))   > 0)
               as.data.frame(ora_up)   %>% arrange(p.adjust) %>%
               slice_head(n = top_n)  %>% mutate(direction = "Upregulated") else NULL
  df_down <- if (!is.null(ora_down) && nrow(as.data.frame(ora_down)) > 0)
               as.data.frame(ora_down) %>% arrange(p.adjust) %>%
               slice_head(n = top_n)  %>% mutate(direction = "Downregulated") else NULL

  df <- bind_rows(df_up, df_down)
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)

  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      GeneRatio_num = sapply(GeneRatio, function(x) {
        p <- strsplit(x, "/")[[1]]; as.numeric(p[1]) / as.numeric(p[2])
      }),
      # GO term names for the paper: first letter capitalised (GO uses all
      # lower case), except terms starting with an abbreviation such as
      # rRNA / tRNA / mRNA (second letter already upper case), which stay as is
      Description = ifelse(grepl("^[a-z][A-Z]", Description), Description,
                           paste0(toupper(substr(Description, 1, 1)),
                                  substr(Description, 2, nchar(Description)))),
      Description = str_wrap(Description, width = 50),
      direction   = factor(direction, levels = c("Upregulated", "Downregulated")),
      Description = reorder(Description, GeneRatio_num)
    )

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(GeneRatio_num, Description, color = p.adjust, size = Count)) +
    geom_point() +
    facet_grid(direction ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    scale_color_gradient(low = "#C0392B", high = "#2980B9", name = "FDR",
                         limits = c(0, 0.05), oob = scales::squish,
                         labels = scales::label_scientific(digits = 1)) +
    # whole-number breaks only (gene counts are integers)
    scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene count", range = c(2, 7),
                          breaks = function(l) unique(round(scales::pretty_breaks(n = 4)(l)))) +
    labs(title = clade_label, x = "Gene ratio", y = NULL) +
    pub_theme +
    # bigger axis text than pub_theme: GO term names (bold), gene-ratio ticks and title
    theme(axis.text.y      = element_text(size = PUB_AXIS, face = "bold", color = "black"),
          axis.text.x      = element_text(size = PUB_AXIS, face = "bold", angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, color = "black"),
          axis.title.x     = element_text(size = PUB_AXIS, face = "bold",  color = "black"),
          strip.text.y     = element_text(size = PUB_SIZE, face = "bold", color = "white", angle = 90),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey30", color = NA),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey90"),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right")

  g          <- ggplotGrob(p)
  strip_idx  <- which(grepl("strip-r", g$layout$name))
  strip_fill <- c("Upregulated" = "#C0392B", "Downregulated" = "#2471A3")
  present_dirs <- levels(droplevels(df$direction))

  for (i in seq_along(strip_idx)) {
    fill_col      <- strip_fill[present_dirs[i]]
    rect_grob_idx <- which(sapply(g$grobs[[strip_idx[i]]]$grobs[[1]]$children,
                                  function(ch) inherits(ch, "rect")))
    g$grobs[[strip_idx[i]]]$grobs[[1]]$children[[rect_grob_idx]]$gp$fill <- fill_col
  }
  # every GO term gets the same row height on the y axis, so the saved figure
  # must give each row room for the tallest (most-wrapped) term
  attr(g, "n_terms")   <- nrow(df)
  attr(g, "max_lines") <- max(str_count(as.character(df$Description), "\n") + 1)
  g
}
```

---

## Step 15. Per-clade volcano and GO dot plots

Iterates over all clades with at least 5 DEGs, generates a volcano plot and GO dot plot for each using the functions defined in Step 14, prints them inline, and saves each as a 600 dpi TIFF named after the clade. Clades with no significant GO terms are noted in the console.

```{r fig.width = 10, fig.height = 9}
clade_deg_counts <- dge_combined %>%
  filter(direction != "NS") %>%
  dplyr::count(clade, name = "n_deg") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_deg))

clades_with_degs <- clade_deg_counts %>% filter(n_deg >= 5) %>% pull(clade)
cat("Saving plots for", length(clades_with_degs), "clades\n\n")

clean_filename <- function(clade_name) {
  clade_name %>%
    str_replace_all("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_") %>%
    str_replace_all("_+", "_") %>%
    str_remove("^_|_$")
}

for (cl in clades_with_degs) {
  fn <- clean_filename(cl)
  cat("Processing:", cl, "->", fn, "\n")

  v <- plot_volcano(dge_results[[cl]], clade_label = cl)
  print(v)
  # compact figure, 600 dpi TIFF + vector PDF for the paper
  ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("volcano_", fn, ".tiff")),
         v, width = 7, height = 6, units = "in",
         dpi = 600, device = "tiff", compression = "lzw")
  ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("volcano_", fn, ".pdf")),
         v, width = 7, height = 6, units = "in", device = cairo_pdf)

  g <- plot_go_dotplot(ora_results[[cl]]$up, ora_results[[cl]]$down, clade_label = cl)
  if (!is.null(g)) {
    grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(g)
    # height = title/axis space + one row per GO term; each row fits the
    # tallest (most-wrapped) term: about 0.26 in per text line at 18 pt + a gap
    go_height <- max(4, 1.8 + attr(g, "n_terms") * (0.26 * attr(g, "max_lines") + 0.12))
    ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("GO_dotplot_", fn, ".tiff")),
           g, width = 10, height = go_height, units = "in",
           dpi = 600, device = "tiff", compression = "lzw")
    # vector PDF (text stays editable/sharp for the paper figure)
    ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("GO_dotplot_", fn, ".pdf")),
           g, width = 10, height = go_height, units = "in", device = cairo_pdf)
  } else {
    cat("  No significant GO terms for:", cl, "\n")
  }
}

cat("\nDone. Files saved to:", OUT_DIR, "\n")
```

## Step 16. GSEA per clade

Complements the ORA above by running gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) on all tested genes ranked by signed significance (sign(log2FC) × −log10(padj)), which can detect coordinated modest shifts invisible to threshold-based ORA. Clades with fewer than 100 tested genes are skipped. Results are combined, written to CSV, and summarized by clade and direction.

```{r}
# library(clusterProfiler)

# run_gsea <- function(res_df, min_genes = 100) {

#

#     filter(!is.na(padj), !is.na(log2FoldChange), padj > 0) %>%
#     mutate(stat_rank = sign(log2FoldChange) * -log10(padj)) %>%
#     arrange(desc(stat_rank))
```

## Step 17. GSEA leading-edge gene analysis and volcano overlay

Extracts the leading-edge genes (core_enrichment field) from each GSEA hit and annotates them with their DESeq2 results to show where they land relative to the DEG thresholds. Quantifies how many leading-edge genes per clade were invisible to ORA (below padj/LFC thresholds). Defines `plot_volcano_gsea()` to highlight leading-edge genes on the volcano with a second color layer, then generates one such plot per clade with GSEA hits. A faceted grid across all GSEA clades (4 per row) is also produced for an overview. Source data tables are written to file.
